findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_site, list_sites, agent_seats, get_upgrade_link, list_versions, list_webhooks · Private data: publish_site, update_site, get_site, list_sites, delete_site, rotate_token, revoke_token, agent_seats, whoami, get_upgrade_link, claim_share_credit, list_versions, restore_version, add_domain, list_domains, remove_domain, domain_status, plan_upload, finalize_upload, get_manifest, site_analytics, site_visits, set_site_access, set_listing, set_badge, create_webhook, list_webhooks, delete_webhook · Public sink: publish_site, update_site, revoke_token, agent_seats, get_upgrade_link, claim_share_credit, list_versions, add_domain, domain_status, plan_upload, finalize_upload, create_webhook, list_webhooks, delete_webhook · Destructive: publish_site, update_site, delete_site, get_upgrade_link, claim_share_credit, remove_domain, plan_upload, site_analytics, delete_webhook.

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
